»

»
 Pendulums
»
 9050 Pendulum Impact Testing System
 9050 Pendulum Impact Testing System
The Instron 9050 pendulum impact tester determines the impact resilience of plastics and composites safely and efficiently. It complies with all major ISO and ASTM impact testing methods, covering an energy range of 0.5 to 50 J and supporting Charpy, Izod, and tensile impact testing.
 Charpy, Izod, and Tensile Impact Testing
Charpy, Izod, and tensile pendulum impact tests are the most common methods for determining a material's impact strength. Understanding a material's energy absorption properties is critical — it predicts the level of plastic deformation the material can withstand before failure. While Izod and Charpy testing measure similar properties, crack propagation differs between the two due to differences in specimen design and testing configuration.
Charpy Impact Test
Izod Pendulum Impact Test
Tensile Pendulum Impact Test
SIMPLER
Efficient Testing
Ergonomic Hammer and Specimen Support Setup - The ergonomic setup of the hammers and specimen supports lets users work safely and efficiently.
Fast Energy and Configuration Changes - Switching between high (50 J) and low (0.5 J) energy hammers, and between Charpy and Izod configurations, is quick and straightforward.
Integrated Control Panel -The integrated touch panel PC puts testing control at your fingertips, with an extensive set of test parameters stored for prompt use to maximize lab efficiency.
Double Braking Mechanism - The manual pendulum's hammer disk brake delivers high torque with low operator effort, with a double braking surface positioned for smooth, convenient operation.
SMARTER
Advanced Performances
Tester Display - The touch panel PC displays critical information, such as percentage of absorbed energy, ensuring each test runs according to the applicable testing standard.
Patented Hammer Design - The one-piece patented hammer structure is specifically designed to reduce energy lost to vibration, delivering exceptional rigidity and superior accuracy.
Advanced Software - Optional software adds value to results and enables post-test data export — from professional reports with graphs and tables to customized text files.
Thermal Conditioning Chamber - The optional thermal conditioning chamber encloses the specimen vice, ensuring fast time-to-impact when testing at low temperatures.
SAFER
Stiff Frame for Better Reliability
Reduced Manual Errors - Advanced electronics automatically recognize the mounted hammer and retrieve its relevant data from the internal database, eliminating the risk of manual data entry errors.
Accurate Energy Values - Accurate energy values require a robust, monolithic frame structure paired with a precise, non-contacting magnetic encoder that ensures zero friction — both of which the Instron 9050 is built around.
Enhanced User Protection - Safety guards prevent unwanted access to the test area, ensuring maximum operator protection.
Safe, Wire-Free Hammer Setup - All instrumented hammers are wire-free, eliminating downtime from hammer connection setup and the risk of wire damage.
Accessories and Options
 Pendulum Impact Hammers
A range of interchangeable hammers covering the full 0.5–50 J energy range, automatically recognized by the system's electronics for fast, error-free configuration changes.
More Info 
 Vice and Specimen Supports
Ergonomically designed specimen supports and vices for secure, repeatable specimen positioning across Charpy, Izod, and tensile configurations.
More Info 
 Software
Optional advanced software for post-test data export, professional reporting, and customized data output.
More Info 
 Specimen Preparation
Punching machines create specimens using interchangeable steel dies with hand-finished cutting edges, supporting specimen preparation to ISO 179, ISO 180, ASTM D256, ASTM D638, and other major standards.
More Info 
 Low Temperature Impact Testing
Low-Temperature Impact Testing Supports impact testing at reduced temperatures when paired with the optional thermal conditioning chamber.
More Info 
 Pendulum Reinforced Table
Firmly fixes the pendulum for maximum stability, minimizing vibration for reliable results — especially useful with high-energy hammers (25–50 J). Includes drawers for collecting broken specimens and storing tools and documents.
More Info 
 Talk to an Instron Expert.
Not sure which Instron 9050 configuration fits your impact testing needs? Tell us about your application and we will help you find the right solution.

Impact, Rheology, and Thermomechanical Testing Systems
 Products
»
 Testing Systems
»
 Impact, Rheology, and Thermomechanical Testing Systems
Instron offers a range of testing systems for evaluating melt flow behavior, rheological properties, heat deflection temperature (HDT), and the Vicat softening temperature of plastics, in addition to characterizing impact resistance for a variety of materials and components.
 Impact Drop Towers & Pendulums
Impact resistance is one of the most important properties for component designers to consider. Impact resistance is a critical measure of service life, and it involves the perplexing problem of product safety and liability.
More Info 
 Rheometers and Melt Flow Testers
The Instron line of rheology testing systems are used to measure the rheological properties of thermoplastics to characterize the polymer melt flow behavior in the process conditions.
More Info 
 HDT & Vicat
HDT and Vicat systems are used to characterize the behavior of plastic materials at high temperatures, measuring the heat deflection temperature (HDT) and the Vicat softening temperature.
More Info

Testing Accessories
 Products
»
 Testing Accessories
Leveraging deep applications experience and engineering expertise, Instron provides a comprehensive range of accessories for materials testing systems. Our portfolio includes hundreds of grips, fixtures, load cells, and application‑specific solutions engineered to support accurate, repeatable testing across a wide variety of materials and standards. Pair these accessories with our testing software for full control over test setup, execution, and analysis. Choose a category below, view the interactive accessories catalog(opens in new tab), or download a PDF version(opens in new tab) to get started.
 Load Cells
Load cells convert the force experienced by the specimen into an electrical signal used by the electronic controller to precisely monitor, report, and control the applied force. Instron designs and manufactures its own load cells — ensuring accuracy, compatibility, and traceability across the full range of Instron testing systems.
Learn More 
 Extensometers
Extensometry provides a direct and accurate method for measuring and controlling specimen deformation by monitoring strain over a precisely defined gauge length. Instron offers contacting and non-contacting extensometers for static, dynamic, and high-temperature applications.
Learn More 
 Chambers and Furnaces
Environmental chambers and furnaces provide the capability to study the mechanical properties of materials and components across a wide temperature range — from sub-zero cryogenic conditions through to +1,600°C — for applications where temperature has a critical influence on material behavior.
Learn More 
 Tensile Grips
A wide range of tensile grip styles and force capacities for holding diverse materials including thread, rope, rubber, plastics, composites, fasteners, sheet metal, and more. Each grip type is engineered for secure, consistent specimen clamping to minimize slippage and ensure accurate results.
Learn More 
 Compression Platens
Compression platens and anvils in a range of sizes and force capacities — from rigid foam and packaging materials through to concrete cylinders, cubes, and high-strength structural specimens.
Learn More 
 Flex Fixtures
Three and four-point bend fixtures for determining the stiffness, yield, and flexural strength of plastics, metals, composites, and similar rigid materials to ASTM, ISO, and EN standards.
Learn More 
 Peel, Friction, Puncture
Fixtures for performing peel, puncture, burst, and coefficient of friction tests on adhesives, films, foils, packaging, and coated materials to a wide range of industry standards.
Learn More 
 Torsion Add-On
The Torsion Add-On 3.0 can be installed on any new or existing 6800 or 5900 Series universal testing system to enable simultaneous axial and torsional testing of components such as bone screws, Luer locks, electrical knobs, and more.
Learn More 
 AT2 Automated XY Stage
The AT2 can be added to any new or existing 6800 or 5900 Series system to automate compression, tensile, and flexure testing of devices or components with multiple test points or repetitive test locations — widely used in biomedical and electronics testing.
Learn More 
 Frame Accessories
Load frame accessories designed to fit specific Instron testing frames — including support tables, protective debris shields, T-slot tables, in-head wedge grips, in-head tension rods, and more.
Learn More 
 Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Fixtures
Fixtures and accessories for testing medical devices, drug delivery systems, surgical instruments, implants, and pharmaceutical packaging — supporting compliance with ISO, ASTM, and regulatory requirements for biomedical and healthcare applications.
Learn More 
 Electronics and Microelectronics Fixtures
Grips, fixtures, and system add-ons for tension, compression, flexure, peel, shear, and puncture testing of electronic components, PCBs, connectors, and microelectronic devices.
Learn More 
 Battery Testing Solutions
Accessories for testing the mechanical properties of materials, adhesives, welds, and components found in battery cells, modules, and packs — supporting the development and quality control of battery systems for electric vehicles, consumer electronics, and energy storage applications.
Learn More 
 Composite Fixtures
Fixtures for tension, compression, flexure, shear, and peel testing of composite materials — most designed to meet specific ASTM, ISO, and EN composite testing standards.
Learn More 
 Couplings and Adapters
Couplings and adapters modify the test system's connection type, allowing you to interface with a wider range of grips and fixtures across different clevis, threaded, and flanged connection types.
Learn More 
 Fastener Fixtures
Fixtures designed for fast and accurate tensile testing of bolts, screws, studs, and nuts — including proof load, wedge tensile, and cone stripping test configurations to ASTM F606 and related standards.
Learn More 
 Test Plates
T-slot tables and component test plates for mounting or clamping components, structures, and assemblies for tensile, compression, bend, peel, and puncture testing.
Learn More 
 Food Testing Fixtures
Fixtures covering a wide range of industry-standard food texture testing methods — including compression, puncture, shear, and extrusion tests for evaluating the texture, firmness, and consistency of food products.
Learn More 
 Wood Fixtures
Fixtures for testing wood and wood-based products for adhesive bond strength, compression, bend strength, shear, and tensile strength to standard and application-specific test methods.
Learn More 
 Crash Simulation Accessories
Accessories for low-speed rear, side, and pole impact simulation — supporting the development and validation of automotive safety systems with improved productivity and testing efficiency.
Learn More 
 Alignment Fixtures
Fixtures and software for measuring and adjusting load string alignment in real time — essential for applications where testing standards specify alignment requirements, such as Nadcap and ISO 23788.
Learn More 
 Specimen Measuring and Preparation
Solutions for specimen cutting, marking, and dimensional measurement — ensuring correct specimen geometry and consistency for accurate and repeatable test results.
Learn More 
 Out of Production Accessories
A listing of major accessories for Instron testing systems that are no longer in production — including environmental chambers, extensometers, tensile grips, and hydraulic grip pumps — with information on available alternatives and upgrade paths.
Learn More 
 Out of Production Specimen Preparation and Measuring Devices
A listing of notching machines, punching machines, and other specimen preparation devices that are no longer in production, with guidance on available alternatives.
Learn More 
 Talk to an Instron Expert
Not finding the accessory you need? Instron has developed thousands of custom grips, fixtures, and accessories — many of which are not listed in our standard catalog. Tell us about your application and we will help you find the right solution.

 Impact Testing
 Impact Testing
Impact testing measures a material’s ability to withstand sudden, high‑speed forces, providing a clear picture of how it absorbs energy and ultimately fails. By capturing this behavior under rapid loading, engineers gain essential insight into toughness, durability, and real‑world performance. These tests help predict how a product will respond to impacts in service, whether it is a structural component, a consumer product, or a safety‑critical part, making impact testing a key step in designing stronger and more reliable materials.
 Why is Impact Testing Important?
Impact resistance is one of the most important properties for a part designer to consider, and without question, the most difficult to quantify. The impact resistance of a part is, in many applications, a critical measure of service life. More importantly these days, it involves the perplexing problem of product safety and liability.
One must determine:
The impact energies the part can be expected to see in its lifetime
The type of impact that will deliver that energy, and then
Select a material that will resist such assaults over the projected life span
Molded-in stresses, polymer orientation, weak spots (e.g. weld lines or gate areas), and part geometry will affect impact performance. Impact properties also change when additives, e.g. coloring agents, are added to plastics.
Molded-in stresses, polymer orientation, weak spots (e.g. weld lines or gate areas), and part geometry will affect impact performance. Impact properties also change when additives, e.g. coloring agents, are added to plastics.
 Ductile vs. Brittle
Most real world impacts are biaxial rather than unidirectional.
Further complication is offered by the choice of failure modes: ductile or brittle. Brittle materials take little energy to start a crack, little more to propagate it to a shattering climax. Other materials possess ductility to varying degrees. Highly ductile materials fail by puncture in drop weight testing and require a high energy load to initiate and propagate the crack.
Many materials are capable of either ductile or brittle failure, depending upon the type of test and rate and temperature conditions. They possess a ductile/brittle transition that actually shifts according to these variables.
 What Testing Equipment is critical for Impact Test results
Pendulum Impact Testing machines and Drop Weight Testers are both critical to validating the performance of materials. However, there are differences between the two instruments that determine which application is best suited to each
 Difference between a Pendulum Impact Testing machine and a Drop Weight Tester
Each test uses a different approach.
As the name implies, a pendulum uses a hammer (mass) rotating on an axis to strike a sample. The point of impact occurs at the lowest point of the pendulum arc when the force is only directed in the horizontal plane.
In a drop weight tester, a mass is dropped on a sample, and the impact is measured using a load cell. The force of impact is directed in the vertical plane only. Unlike pendulums, drop towers can also measure deformation, thus giving more information about the material properties.
The first step to determining whether to use a pendulum or a drop tower is knowing the standards that the test needs to comply with.
There are two traditional standards for measuring impact resistance: the Charpy pendulum impact test (ISO 179/ASTM D6110) and the Izod test (ISO 180/ASTM D256). These two test methods are used to certify the impact resistance of a variety of materials, including metals as well as plastics, resins, and composites. They are often found on data sheets to show that the material conforms to its specifications.
Neither Charpy nor Izod test standards allow for the use of drop towers except for the ISO 179-2 standard. This limitation means that only pendulum impact testers may be used to certify products according to ISO 179-1/ASTM D6110 and/or ISO 180/ASTM D256.
Drop Weight testers can still be used to perform Charpy and Izod tests for internal purposes (e.g., to compare products or investigate material properties). Not only that. Drop towers offer greater flexibility than pendulums when it comes to testing configurations and can test according to a variety of standards, including:
ISO11343 – Adhesives – Peel Impact Test Method
ISO 8256 – Determination of Tensile Impact Test
ISO 6603-2 and ASTM D3763 - Puncture Resistance of Plastic
ASTM D7136 - Compression After Impact
Drop towers can also be used to perform component tests that go beyond the requirements of international standards.

 Impact Testing Systems
Impact resistance is one of the most important properties for component designers to consider, and one of the most difficult to quantify. It's a critical measure of service life and carries significant implications for product safety and liability. Instron has more than 80 years of experience designing impact testing systems that simulate real-life impact conditions.
 Drop Weight Impact Testers
Instron Drop Towers are used to develop, fine-tune, and validate material models under high-rate impact conditions. The new 9400 Series produces reliable, repeatable results, whether you're testing materials and components before production to improve product acceptance or testing during production to ensure continuous improvement.
Drop weight testing is commonly used across automotive, packaging, consumer electronics, and materials research applications to evaluate how a product or material responds to a single, high-energy impact event — from a dropped phone to a vehicle component in a collision. Configurable drop height and impact mass let you tailor tests to a wide range of energy levels and specimen types, supporting standards such as ASTM D3763 and ISO 6603.
More Info 
 Pendulum Testers
Instron Pendulum Impact Testing Systems determine the impact resilience of plastics and composites safely and efficiently, complying with all major ISO and ASTM impact testing methods across an energy range of 0.5 to 50 J. It supports Charpy, Izod, and tensile impact testing in both manual and motorized configurations, making it well suited to quality control and material characterization work where repeatable, standards-compliant results are essential.
Unlike drop weight testing, which simulates a single high-energy impact event, pendulum impact testing measures the energy absorbed by a specimen during fracture — a key indicator of a material's toughness and resistance to sudden loading.
More Info 
 Out of Production Impact Drop Towers & Pendulums
All impact Instron Impact Testing systems produced from 1975. These include drop towers and pendulums, such as the Fractovis and Dynatup Series.
